ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, Sept. 12, 2001, as amended, particularly Article 5-2 on customer due diligence and beneficial owner identification); Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 33851, Dec. 22, 2023); Financial Services Commission Notice titled Regulations on Customer Identification and Beneficial Ownership Verification; Commercial Act (Act No. 17905, Aug. 8, 2023) regarding corporate records, shareholder registers, and registered officers; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 17879, June 15, 2022) imposing reporting and identifier requirements for foreign investors; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (Act No. 18596, Sept. 24, 2022).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court in the jurisdiction where the foreign investor or parent company is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PATH A (Hague Apostille Convention state): notarize the original certificate before a qualified local notary, then affix an Apostille certificate from the designated competent authority of that state, and present to the Republic of Korea. PATH B (non-Apostille state): notarize, authenticate at the local foreign-affairs ministry, and legalize at the Consular Section of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction. Use PATH A or PATH B only; the two methods are parallel and mutually exclusive and never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Office or Companies Registry authority of the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PATH A (Hague Apostille Convention state): notarize and apostille by the local competent authority. PATH B (non-Apostille state): notarize, authenticate through the local ministry, and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are alternative and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent company or beneficial owner, notarized in the jurisdiction of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PATH A (Hague Apostille Convention state): notarization followed by apostille. PATH B (non-Apostille state): notarization, internal foreign-affairs authentication, and consular legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea. Never chain both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company of the foreign investor as registered with the competent corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PATH A (Hague Apostille Convention state): certified extract or notarized copy, then apostille by the designated authority. PATH B (non-Apostille state): certified extract authenticated by the local ministry and legalized by the Korean Consulate. These routes are mutually exclusive; do not use both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the corporate account of the investor or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PATH A (Hague Apostille Convention state): original letter signed by bank officer, notarized, and apostilled. PATH B (non-Apostille state): original letter notarized, authenticated by the supervising authority if required, and legalized by the Korean Consulate. The apostille path and consular path are distinct alternatives and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or notary in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PATH A (Apostille Convention state): notarize the officer list and then apostille. PATH B (non-Apostille state): notarize, authenticate in the local foreign-affairs ministry, and legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The two procedures are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, senior managers, and ultimate beneficial owners, including any person holding or controlling 25% or more of shares, voting rights, or decision-making power, must be completed before incorporation and repeated at least every 90 days. Screening must be run against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit under the Financial Services Commission PEP database, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Korea's domestic sanctions list issued under the Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction, and all EU and US advisory lists. Automated negative-news CRC tools with real-time updates are required. Any PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media trigger must be resolved in writing by the AML compliance officer before proceeding; enhanced due diligence including source of wealth, source of funds, and documentary verification is mandatory for all high-risk or PEP-matched persons, and any unresolved match must be reported by Suspicious Transaction Report to KOFIU. All records must be retained for at least seven years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS) Name Search and Reservation System - www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be registered in the Korean Hangul script. A Romanized or English trade name may be used in parallel but cannot replace the Hangul registered name for official registry, tax, banking, customs, and court filings. Foreign names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul, and the registered Hangul name must be consistent across all Korean government agencies. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive element unique from other entities active in the same or similar business; (2) an objective description of the business purpose that accords with ISIC 3091 and the micro-mobility manufacturing scope; (3) the legal form designation 'Yuhan Hoesa' or 'LLC' placed at the end; and (4) a mandatory conflict check requiring that the complete name is not identical or misleadingly similar to any existing Korean corporate name, trademark, or famous trade name. The check must be conducted in iROS, the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) trademark database, and the National Tax Service business registry database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed Hangul name is rejected by the Registry Judge, the applicant must first obtain a written statement of the grounds for rejection from the Commercial Registry Division. The applicant may then file a written objection with the same Registry Division within fourteen days of receipt of the rejection notice, attaching corrected name options, a cover letter explaining how the corrected name satisfies the Commercial Act naming requirements, and iROS or KIPO search results proving non-conflict. If the Registry Judge upholds the rejection, an immediate appeal may be filed with the High Court within seven days of the refusal notice. In parallel, where the rejection is based on a trademark conflict, the applicant may apply to KIPO for rectification or cancellation of the conflicting trademark, and any adverse KIPO decision must be appealed to the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board within thirty days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The National Tax Service and licensed Korean banks generally reject virtual offices and commercial mailboxes as insufficient for a manufacturing corporate entity. A Yuhan Hoesa engaged in electric cargo e-bike manufacturing must maintain a physical registered office in Korea that is either owned or leased under a registered lease agreement, with a visible corporate sign, operational telephone line, and actual capability to receive original notices and service of process. Banks performing corporate account onboarding will conduct an on-site visit and will decline account opening if the address is a virtual office or public mailbox. In addition, the local municipal tax office will treat a virtual office as a sham commercial substance and may cancel the Business Registration Certificate, impose administrative fines, and assess corporate income tax on penalties. Accordingly, virtual office and commercial mailbox arrangements are not permissible for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) corporate signboard displayed at the registered address; (2) original lease contract and current utility bills in the company's name; (3) Business Registration Certificate posted; (4) actual production equipment and inventory consistent with electric cargo e-bike manufacturing; (5) presence of employees or a responsible representative during normal business hours; (6) payroll records, tax invoices, and corporate bank statements supporting economic substance; (7) annual customs and factory records consistent with ISIC 3091. Quantified risk: there is a 75% to 90% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the municipal tax authority or the National Tax Service within the first fiscal year for a foreign-owned manufacturing entity. Failure of the inspection may result in deregistration, criminal referral, confiscation of equipment, and tax penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as last amended), specifically Articles 169, 175, 288, 289, 290, 292, 295, 317, 543, 548, 550 and 553, together with the Regulations on Corporate Registration under the Supreme Court Registration of Non-Real Estate Cases Act and the Framework Act on Fiscal and Tax Administration for post-formation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, typically Seoul Central District Court Registration Division, accessed electronically through the Supreme Court of Korea InterNet Registration Office (IRO) at erops.scourt.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited company) under Article 553 of the Commercial Act, together with notarized Articles of Incorporation, certified minutes of the promoters meeting, bank capital deposit certificate, a certificate of corporate seal impression, and the prescribed registration form under corporate registration regulation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None, in the sense that the Korean Commercial Act does not prescribe any statutory minimum contributed capital for a Yuhan Hoesa; however, the Articles of Incorporation must state the total contributed capital, and every contribution, whether cash or in kind, must be fully paid or delivered before incorporation registration. The capital subscription funds must be deposited in a blocked capital deposit account at a licensed commercial bank and remain blocked until the court registry accepts the incorporation, after which they may be released to the operating account; inbound foreign subscriptions must be credited through a foreign exchange bank and reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA, A KOREAN LIMITED COMPANY IN FORMATION. 1. ORGANIZATION AND QUORUM. The undersigned initial directors, duly appointed in writing by the promoters of Yuhan Hoesa, constitute the initial board of directors for the limited purpose of organizing the Company and authorizing all steps required for statutory incorporation, corporate governance, and banking arrangements. 2. APPROVAL OF ARTICLES. RESOLVED, that the board adopts, ratifies, and approves the Articles of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa in the form previously circulated to the promoters, including the corporate name, the total contributed capital, the registered office at the address supplied to the registry, the corporate object of designing, manufacturing, assembling, painting, testing, warehousing, and exporting urban electric cargo bicycles and step-through scooters, and the governance rules of a limited company governed by the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. 3. CONFIRMATION OF CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the board confirms that each initial contributor has subscribed the number of contribution units stated in the shareholders contribution ledger and that the total paid-in amount has been received by the company-designated bank and is evidenced by the capital deposit certificate; the board directs the representative director to keep the deposit blocked until the court registry has entered the incorporation. 4. REGISTERED OFFICE AND SEAL. RESOLVED, that the board designates the address in the Articles as the Company's registered office, adopts the corporate seal and authenticated financial seal, and authorizes the representative director to file the corporate seal impression and the seal certificate with the registry, banks, and government agencies. 5. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the board authorizes Yuhan Hoesa to open general operating accounts, segregated escrow accounts if required by counterparties, and foreign exchange accounts with licensed commercial banks in Korea; any two of the representative director, the finance director, or another board-appointed approved signatory shall sign or electronically authorize all account mandates, wire release instructions, loan documents, guarantees, and treasury settlement operations; in no event shall one signatory act without a co-signatory. 6. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that the board appoints the representative director to act as the company's legal representative for all corporate, judicial, tax, and licensing matters, and appoints a company secretary and a finance officer as statutory officers, with authority to prepare, file, witness, and coordinate all registration and license applications. 7. AUTHORIZATION OF INCORPORATION EXPENSES. RESOLVED, that the board ratifies and authorizes the representative director to pay registration fees, notarial fees, translation fees, professional fees, and reasonable formation expenses out of corporate funds, and to enter into service agreements with attorneys, accountants, and tax agents as needed. 8. MINUTES AND EFFECTIVENESS. RESOLVED, that this resolution is effective immediately, shall be recorded in the corporate minute book, and may be certified by the company secretary as a true corporate record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea InterNet Registration Office (IRO) at erops.scourt.go.kr; notarization by a Korean notary public or the notary section of the district prosecutors/public attorneys office that has jurisdiction over the promoters residence or the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the Korean corporate registry name database to confirm that Yuhan Hoesa does not conflict with an existing registered trade name in the same business category, and reserve the legal name if requested. Thereafter prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, stating the corporate object to include the manufacture and assembly of electric cargo bicycles, step-through scooters and related micro-mobility parts, battery modules and accessories; the total contributed capital; the registered office address; the class and number of contribution units; transfer restrictions; accounting period; and number of directors. Have the Articles signed by every promoter and notarized by an authorized Korean notary, because the court registry will reject an unnotarized original. The notary must attest the authenticity of signature and corporate purpose. The company name should also be registered in the Korean trademark and civil classification if local protection is desired, although separate from statutory formation.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID card of each promoter and anticipated director
Certificate of personalized seal or power of attorney if a proxy signs
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Korean, notarized copy
Name availability check printout or name reservation reference number
Registered office address proof such as lease agreement, ownership certificate, or consent of owner for registration address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name check or notary office raises a conflict or defect, file an amended name or execute an amended notarized signature page and resubmit the corrected Articles for notarization; IRO name reservations can be changed without refund penalty, and the corrected document can be re-filed before the 14-day registry suspension window closes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of capital contribution and obtaining blocked deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in Korea, typically the bank that will later serve as the main operating bank for Yuhan Hoesa; with the foreign exchange desk of the same bank coordinating any inbound foreign equity remittance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the promoters have signed the notarized Articles, the representative director nominee opens a temporary capital contribution deposit account in the name of Yuhan Hoesa, or in the name of the promoters in trust for the future company, as the bank instructs. Each promoter transfers the subscribed cash contribution into this account, ensuring that the total balance equals the contributed capital stated in the Articles. For in-kind contributions, the promoter must deliver the asset to the company-designated receiver and obtain an independent valuation certificate or court-appointed asset appraisal if requested. The bank then issues a corporate capital deposit certificate and, where deposits originate abroad, an inbound remittance certificate stating source and purpose. Those certificates form the conclusive proof of payment for the court registration. Funds remain in the blocked account until incorporation is entered in the court registry; after delivery of the certificate of registration, the same bank can release funds to a corporate operating account under the corporate seal mandate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate name reservation or draft corporate registration number
Identity documents and corporate photo for each account signatory and promoter
Capital payment schedule showing subscriber, units, amount and date
Inbound remittance certificate and source-of-funds declaration for each foreign subscriber
Company formation passport or company registration abstract for corporate subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank treats the temporary account as a personal account and queries identity or source of funds, the promoters must resubmit current passport size photos and the bank beneficial ownership statement. If the deposit certificate is refused because the remittance is from a high-risk jurisdiction, the bank will request enhanced beneficial ownership declarations and proof of business purpose; these can be cured by supplying the supply contract or invoice from the e-bike OEM project and a certificate of residence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of incorporation with the district court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar at the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division; online filing through the Supreme Court IRO electronic filing portal under the Regulations on the Electronic Registration of Non-Real Estate Cases.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic application for incorporation registration of a Yuhan Hoesa through the IRO portal, selecting the district court with local jurisdiction where the registered office is located. Attach the application captioned Application for Incorporation Registration of a Limited Company, the notarized Articles, minutes of the promoters meeting containing the directors appointment, the capital deposit certificate, and proof of registration tax payment with local education surcharge. Each initial director must submit a statement of acceptance and consent. The registrar verifies the legality of the corporate object, the adequacy of the description of the business as manufacturer of electric bicycles under ISIC 3091, the correctness of capital payment, the identity of signatories, and the statutory governance features. Once approved, the court assigns the corporate registration number and opens the corporate register; the company then exists as a juristic person on the date of registration. The representative director should print the certified corporate registration certificate at the court after issuance, and the original documents remain in the court archive.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration signed by representative director or proxy
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the promoters meeting, including the election of initial directors
Bank capital deposit certificate and valuation report for in-kind contributions if any
Consent forms signed by each director and auditor confirming appointment
Proof of registration tax and local education surcharge payment
Power of attorney if filing is through a certified administrative lawyer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order for defects, file the cured documents within the statutory cure period, generally one to 14 days, through e-return submission. If the defect is capital proof or notarial attestation, obtain a corrected bank certificate or re-notarized Articles and resubmit; if the registrar rejects the corporate object as too broad, pass a formal amendment of Articles at the promoters meeting and file the amended notarized version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, business license issuance, and social insurance post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district office having jurisdiction over the registered office through the HomeTax electronic portal; the Korea VAT and corporate income tax registration desk; the local municipal civil service office; and the four major social insurance institutions coordinated through the Korea Employment Information Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration certificate is obtained, begin operational licensing and tax registration without delay. File startup business registration with the National Tax Service using the corporate registration number, entering the corporate object, registered office, and business hours; the NTS will issue the business registration certificate that is required for VAT invoices, customs exports, bank account finalization, and hiring employees. Register the corporate seal with the bank and amend the temporary contribution account into the corporate operating account. If the factory employs workers, complete registration with the national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance systems, and file the corporate tax return under the Tax Adjustment Act. Application for customs import and export unique business code should be submitted to the Korea Customs Service if the company will directly import battery cells or components or export finished cargo e-bikes. A physical site inspection may be conducted by NTS or the municipality to confirm the planned factory address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration from the district court
Business registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and corporate seal certificate
Registered office lease agreement or proof of factory site ownership
Director passports and appointment minutes
Bank account proof and capital deposit certificate
Export and import registration application if international trade is intended
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS suspends or delays issuance because of a mismatch between corporate purpose and factory establishment certification, fix the e-business classification code and submit the factory establishment approval or report in progress. If a foreign director does not have an alien registration card, the NTS can accept a residence registration equivalent from the foreign ministry or registry office and the director should obtain a business managing certificate; the tax office can issue an interim business registration certificate while documentation is perfected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy; the regional and city-county district authority that issues factory establishment approval or factory establishment report under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act; Korea Industrial Complex Corporation for consultation on factory siting; the Ministry of Environment and regional environmental office for discharges and emissions; and the Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety in manufacturing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Certificate or Factory Establishment Report Approval for the electric cargo bicycle and step-through scooter manufacturing plant under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act, together with an industrial facility operation permit and a Clean Air Conservation Act permit for painting and coating operations; a Water Environment Conservation Act permit for cooling water or cleaning-process wastewater discharge if discharge thresholds are exceeded.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the local Regional Environmental Office having jurisdiction over the project site, with submission made through the Environmental Impact Assessment Support System operated by the Korea Environment Institute.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report where the factory building floor area is at or above 10,000 square meters or the project fits the EIA Act schedule for industrial complex development; otherwise, a Prior Environmental Review and Site Suitability Review will be applicable. For most departmental manufacturing facilities and small-to-medium assembly plants of less than 10,000 square meters, the Ministry of Environment classifies the operation as an Environmental Registration and Compliance Filing project, but the factory would still require air pollutant emission facility registration, wastewater discharge facility registration, and waste generation notification under the respective environmental media acts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from electroplating, washing and battery forming processes, if covered, must meet the national effluent limits of biochemical oxygen demand at or below 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand at or below 40 mg/L, total suspended solids at or below 40 mg/L, total nitrogen at or below 60 mg/L, total phosphorus at or below 8 mg/L and pH between 5.8 and 8.6. Spray coating and paint curing emissions must be routed through pollution-control equipment and comply with volatile organic compound concentration limits at the stack of not more than 500 ppm measured as total hydrocarbons, unless an individual air permit prescribes a stricter limit; workplace atmospheric exposure limits for benzene, toluene and xylene shall remain at or below 1 ppm, 50 ppm and 100 ppm respectively. Hazardous waste, including spent lithium battery cells, paint sludge, waste solvents and solvent-containing absorbents, must be segregated, stored on impermeable sealed drainage surfaces, manifested, and delivered to registered hazardous waste treatment facilities within 90 days unless the seventy-day storage extension for small quantity generators is granted.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), with the principal electronic administrative platform being the HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr. Customs and export clearance matters are processed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal at portal.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly formed Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC must apply for business registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its statutory place of business. The application is filed on HomeTax using the Application for Business Registration; the NTS then issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) which functions simultaneously as the corporate Tax Identification Number and the VAT registration number. Required supporting documents include the articles of incorporation, certificate of capital subscription or paid-in capital, representative identification, and evidence of local physical business premises. For a foreign non-resident entity that has not yet formed a Korean local subsidiary but begins carrying on a taxable Korean business through a branch or domestic place of business, the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative, submit an apostilled or notarized certificate of foreign incorporation, its constitutional documents, evidence of a Korean place of business, and a power of attorney authorizing the domestic tax representative, after which the NTS will issue the same BRN/TIN. The registration covers VAT, corporate income tax filing, electronic tax invoice issuance, and employee withholding withholding registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no check-the-box pass-through election under Korean domestic tax law; Yuhan Hoesa LLC is mandatorily taxed at the entity level on its worldwide income as a domestic corporation. A qualifying domestic parent-subsidiary group may voluntarily elect the Korean Consolidated Corporate Income Tax Return System under the Corporate Tax Act, but this is an income-pooling election and does not change the separate entity classification. No elective hybrid mismatch treatment is available; the OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules are implemented mandatorily through the Adjustment of International Trade Tax Act and apply without elective override.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover exemption below which VAT registration is unavailable. Any business operator that starts a trade, business, or revenue-generating activity in Korea must register with the NTS within 20 days of the business commencement date. A simplified taxable person regime may apply to individual businesses whose annual taxable supplies do not exceed KRW 80,000,000, but registration remains mandatory; a corporate Yuhan Hoesa LLC manufacturing electric cargo bikes is a standard taxable person and must register from the first day of business activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean VAT law mandates electronic tax invoicing for all VAT-registered business-to-business supplies. Suppliers must issue an electronic tax invoice by the day following the supply date and transmit the invoice data to the NTS through HomeTax or through an approved electronic tax invoice Application Service Provider (ASP) using certified EDI or API interfaces. The e-tax invoice must contain the supplier and purchaser Business Registration Numbers, supply date, taxable value, VAT amount, and the applicable zero-rating or exemption code. For business-to-consumer cash transactions, the provider must likewise issue and transmit electronic cash receipt data to the NTS in near real time. Korea does not operate a pre-clearance government digital stamping system, but the NTS performs ex-post automated risk matching between electronic tax invoices, VAT returns, customs export declarations, and foreign exchange transaction data; exporters should ensure precise zero-rating reason codes are recorded on each electronic tax invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, such as electric cargo bikes and step-through scooters, qualify for 0% VAT when the goods are physically delivered to a foreign buyer under a Korea Customs Service export declaration and the exporter retains commercial contracts, invoices, loading/transport documents, customs clearance records, and foreign exchange receipt evidence. Qualifying offshore service supplies and digital services supplied to non-resident enterprises also qualify for zero-rating when the services are consumed or effectively used outside Korea, the foreign payor is a non-resident, and the exporter retains documentary proof of the export nature of the supply including contract, service delivery records, and inbound foreign-exchange evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Korea Customs Service electronic export declaration (export B/Entry) evidencing clearance from Korean customs territory
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Korea to the foreign destination with destination country and consignee details
Commercial invoice and packing list fully matching the customs declaration quantity, unit values, and product classification
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or foreign exchange bank purchase/proceeds certificate confirming export proceeds have been repatriated through a Korean foreign exchange bank
Underlying export sales contract or binding purchase order establishing the international sale and foreign purchaser liability
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where the NTS determines that zero-rating was claimed on unsupported, false, or manipulated export documentation, it will issue a deficiency assessment re-imposing VAT at the standard 10% rate together with the statutory additional tax for unreported or under-reported VAT, which may range from 10% to 40% of the unpaid tax depending on intentionality and concealment, plus statutory interest. Penalties may also be imposed for failure to issue or transmit electronic tax invoices and for false export declarations. Criminal liability may be pursued under the Act on Punishment of Tax Evaders, exposing the entity, its directors, and the appointed Korean tax representative to imprisonment for up to three years or criminal fines of up to KRW 30,000,000. The NTS may retrospectively claw back VAT refunds, discontinue zero-rating treatment, and refer documented customs offenses to the Korea Customs Service for parallel administrative or criminal enforcement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (central bank) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (principal authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act), with administrative enforcement by Korea Customs Service and supervision by the Financial Services Commission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-floating foreign exchange market, but capital account convertibility is conditional rather than fully open. Current account transactions are largely liberalized, allowing export/import payments, trade credits, and service fees to flow with minimal friction. Capital account movements, however, require reporting to the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Bank of Korea under designated purpose codes. Non-resident shareholders may convert contributed foreign currency into KRW for operational payments, but profit remittance abroad is subject to a withholding tax clearance certificate issued by the National Tax Service, along with evidence of retained earnings and capital verification. There is no mandatory surrender requirement; exporters may retain foreign exchange earnings in a licensed foreign exchange bank account. However, all transactions exceeding USD 5,000 (or equivalent) must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with specific purpose codes. The Financial Services Commission supervises designated dealing banks; each bank must verify the underlying economic reality to prevent round-tripping. Practical hurdles include strict documentation for dividend distribution, and a bank-issued annual proof of tax compliance before remittance. Currency convertibility is therefore high for current account transactions, moderate for FDI and portfolio inflows, and heavily conditionally controlled for speculative flows or rapid capital withdrawal.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory collection period: export proceeds must be received within 3 years from the date of the export declaration unless the underlying trade contract specifies a shorter term. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% — there is no legal requirement to convert foreign currency receipts into KRW. Export receipts exceeding USD 5,000 must be reported to the authorized dealing bank, and any foreign currency funds held in domestic accounts are subject to annual balance-of-payments reporting to the Bank of Korea.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for foreign digital EMI platforms structured as unlicensed e-money institutions. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, any company providing KRW-denominated corporate payment and collection services must obtain a domestic license or partner with a licensed Korean bank. Global EMI platforms such as Wise only offer multi-currency payout corridors and do not hold Korean Banking Authority approval to service a Korean Yuhan Hoesa's full banking needs. As a result, the treasury blueprint relies exclusively on regulated tier-1 Korean commercial banks for capital escrow, foreign currency pricing, trade settlement, and FX hedging. No fintech EMI is able to replace the statutory foreign exchange reporting and capital verification obligations imposed by Korean regulators.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks generally mandate a physical appearance by the non-resident statutory director at a Korean branch for a face-to-face AML interview and biometric verification. Remote consular proxy opening is only accepted in exceptional low-risk cases and requires a certified apostilled power of attorney, original corporate resolution, passport sample, and a pre-approved remote video interview with a compliance officer. In practice, Shinhan and Woori will allow remote onboarding for a private company if the ultimate beneficial owner is individually identified and a locally resident authorized signatory is appointed, but the foreign director must still send original notarized documents via courier and complete a telephone/video review under internal waiver protocols.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership obscured by multi-layer foreign holding entities or nominee shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete organizational chart showing every intermediate entity up to the individual physical person, audited financial statements of each holding layer, official company registry extracts for the past three years, signed declarations that no nominee arrangements exist, and certified passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection is inconsistent with the manufacturing scale and lacks traceable fund history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of original bank statements from the funding personal or corporate account, a capital contribution declaration certified by an external auditor, tax clearance certificate from the Korean National Tax Service, and purchase orders or letters of intent from prospective OEM buyers substantiating the entity's production plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export trade documentation mismatch between the LC, commercial invoice, and Korea Customs export declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original bills of lading, signed commercial invoices referencing HS code 8711.60 (electric cargo bicycles), Korean export declaration receipts from the Korea Customs Trade Statistics portal, packing lists, and insurance certificates. The bank compliance committee will also require a full exporting agreement that matches the payment terms and product description.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and shareholders show insufficient business substance or unverifiable professional background.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized resumes of all key persons, employer confirmation letters, registration certificates of the parent or related foreign corporations, three years of audited annual accounts for shareholders holding above 10%, and a detailed AML questionnaire explaining business history, customer base, and expected settlement volumes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a prior foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, filed with either KOTRA Invest Korea or a fully licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. After the report is approved, the non-resident shareholder remits funds via SWIFT MT103 to the company's capital escrow account at a designated tier-1 bank. Each payment must include the Korean foreign exchange purpose code for equity participation, and the bank will issue a certificate of capital introduction. Funds must be converted into KRW only after the statutory capital verification is completed by the receiving bank. The Korean bank will also report to the Bank of Korea's balance-of-payments system, and will retain the foreign investment registration documents, the remittance receipt, and the corporate seal registry for the compliance file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for electric cargo e-bike purchases are executed through SWIFT MT103 for telephonic transfers and advance payments, SWIFT MT700/MT707 for documentary letters of credit covering commercial imports and exports, and documentary collection via D/P or D/A through the banks' correspondent clearing networks. When paying foreign suppliers, the Korean company must present a valid tax invoice, an original import declaration from Korea Customs, and a specified trade purpose code. Cross-border disbursements are cleared through the Korean bank's foreign currency clearing network using USD, EUR, or CNY correspondent accounts, subject to Bank of Korea transaction filing for every payment above USD 5,000. KRW is restricted to domestic clearing rails and cannot be used for offshore settlement without prior authorization.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla outright forward contracts with authorized Korean foreign exchange banks, supported by real export/import trade documentation.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between KRW and USD/EUR for trade receivables and verified procurement requirements, executed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for Korean resident companies with actual underlying trade exposure, via an authorized Seoul bank and subject to the bank's net open position limits.
European-style currency options posted on recognized underlying export/import flows, with prohibited use for speculative or naked hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, Local Income Tax Surcharge Return, and Shareholder Ordinary General Meeting Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax) for corporate income tax; competent local government through WeTax for the local income tax surcharge; shareholders of the Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act for financial statement approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each business year, being 31 March for a calendar-year company, with a one-month extension available for calendar-year filers when the final accounts are completed and certified by a tax agent, so that the extended deadline is 30 April; local income tax surcharge filing follows the same national tax deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a 20% negligent non-reporting additional tax and a 40% fraudulent non-reporting additional tax, a 10% understatement penalty, and daily delinquency interest of 0.022% on unpaid amounts; prolonged delinquency enables forced collection, bank/asset seizure, business registration closure by the National Tax Service, and a personal joint liability assessment against the representative where the LLC has insufficient assets; a six-month period of non-payment is the usual administrative trigger for business registration revocation and subsequent dormant-company strike-off procedure before the registration court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filed with the Financial Supervisory Service and Presented at the Annual Shareholders Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system for audit-subject companies; statutory books and submitted auditor report retained at the registered office and presented to the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general meeting and shareholder approval of the separate financial statements must occur no later than three months after the fiscal year-end, or 31 March for calendar-year filers; where an independent audit is mandatory, the auditor's report and audited financial statements must be filed to DART within 15 days after the general meeting and in any event no later than 30 April for calendar-year filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint or file an external auditor results in administrative supervisory measures under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, fines up to KRW 30 million for false financial disclosure, administrative fines up to KRW 5 million for failure to convene the annual meeting, and the audit report may lose evidentiary value before tax and financial institutions, leading to loan acceleration and regulatory denial of the LLC's annual maintenance without causing direct automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Business Report and Event-Based UBO or Shareholding Transfer Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency acting for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy; changes in shareholding or beneficial ownership are also recorded in the register of members at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the foreign-invested enterprise's fiscal year, being 31 March for calendar-year filers; any transfer of membership interest, change in beneficial ownership, change of foreign investor nationality, or capital transfer must be reported to the competent authority within 30 days after the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missed filing of the annual report subjects the company to an administrative fine not exceeding KRW 3 million, loss of the foreign-invested enterprise status and foreign-exchange remittance facilities, and confirmation of the UBO record is frozen; this does not itself cause corporate register strike-off but combined with tax delinquency may be cited in a dormant-company strike-off filed by the registration court.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent audit by an accredited Korean certified public accountant when any of the following quantitative criteria is met at the preceding fiscal year-end: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion; (ii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 7 billion; (iii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and the average number of full-time employees equals or exceeds 300; (iv) the entity is a listed company, financial company, public-interest entity, or large business-group affiliate irrespective of size. Non-listed LLCs below these thresholds are not legally required to obtain an external audit unless required by lenders, investors, or the corporate governance rules of the Yuhan Hoesa's operating agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards are required for listed and public-interest audit-subject companies; a private Yuhan Hoesa not so designated may prepare statutory financial statements under Korean GAAP or K-IFRS, and smaller non-audited enterprises may apply the Korean SME Accounting Standards; the financial statements must comprise a balance sheet, statement of profit or loss, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, and explanatory notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise report is the mandatory annual UBO confirmation vehicle and must verify each foreign member, direct or indirect beneficial owner, shareholding percentage, and any UBO change occurring during the year; under the Korean Commercial Act a transfer of membership interest or economic rights is ineffective against the company and third parties unless recorded in the register of members, and under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be reported to the competent authority within 30 days of the event. There is no separate annual corporate-register renewal form, but anti-money-laundering customer due diligence requires the UBO record to be refreshed for any significant financial transaction or at least annually when the company maintains bank accounts with regulated Korean financial institutions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,800 per year for a full-service registered office, corporate seal, registered agent, annual meeting minutes, and correspondence handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 for a Korean CPA audit of a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa manufacturing electric cargo bicycles near the mandatory audit threshold, with large inventory and stronger internal-control engagements potentially ranging up to USD 40,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal corporate income tax rate applied to taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive rates of 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, and 21% up to KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean Tax Incentive Limitation Act provides R&D credits (up to 25% on qualifying ODM/EV-related R&D, with an incremental-carry-back credit for new growth-source technologies); Foreign Investment Promotion Act free-zone incentives: 100% corporate income tax exemption for 5 years and 50% exemption for 2 further years in designated foreign investment zones; integrated investment tax credit for facility investment in new-growth industries; no standalone patent box, but patent-related IP income can be eligible for R&D credits and SME manufacturing tax reductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return) plus supplementary International Transactions Disclosure Schedule, submitted electronically through HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) under the National Tax Service Unified Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 3 months from the fiscal year-end; for a calendar year-end (31 December) corporation, no later than 31 March of the following year; an additional 1-month extension is available for overseas accounting or audit through the same HomeTax portal

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Identity and Non-Resident Shareholder Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, fiscal year-end, country of incorporation, and detailed schedule of all non-resident shareholders or beneficial owners holding the LLC units.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC is a resident taxpayer even when 100% non-resident owned. Complete every shareholder line with jurisdiction code, percentage ownership, Korean residency certificate status, and a flag for DTA relief claimed. Attach certification that the non-resident shareholder has not engaged in a conduit arrangement for treaty shopping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of Korean GAAP net income before tax to taxable income: add non-deductible expenses, subtract tax-exempt income, deduct loss carryovers, and apply special reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For this micro-mobility OEM, add back intercompany service fees, royalties, and management fees paid to foreign affiliates not supported by arm's length contracts or actual service documentation. Also add back excessive interest applying the Korean thin-capitalization rule (foreign controlling shareholder debt-to-equity cap of 3:1 generally, 2:1 for financial institutions).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of aggregated and counterparty-level related-party transactions: sales of electric cargo e-bikes, component purchases, intercompany loans, intangible royalty flows, and cost-sharing contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the prescribed overseas related-party transaction attachment. Local-file/master-file thresholds under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs are based on total annual intercompany transactions; when the return exceeds the threshold, contemporaneous transfer pricing study, Master File, and Local File must exist by the return due date. A simple declaration without OECD-compliant benchmarking will be treated as non-submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of credit or deduction for foreign income tax paid on foreign-source income entered in gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Article 57 of the Corporate Income Tax Act. The foreign tax credit limit is recomputed per country and is limited to the Korean tax attributable to that country's source income. Retain certified profitability proof and outbound freight/logistics invoices for export sales; if the Korean entity only earns royalty or service income abroad, the FTC schedule must still be supported by evidence of actual withholding in the foreign country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Tax Computation and Local Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax at progressive rates plus 10% local income tax surtax, after credits and minimum tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct withholding tax on non-resident dividends within this box; that is a source obligation of the Korean paying company. If claiming treaty-reduced rates on future profit distribution, confirm that no previously distributed profit has escaped the corporate tax base; otherwise outbound WHT at 22% aggregate is applied and the item is reportable on the non-resident dividend withholding schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Loss Carryforward and Tax Loss Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year operating loss and all historical net losses claimed as carryforwards within the statutory period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean law allows a 10-year carryforward for net losses with strict burden of proof; for a manufacturing LLC, carryforward losses must be traceable to the domestic Korean operations, not to losses of the foreign parent or sister entities. Document title to inventory, export receivables, and plant assets; a loss claim that shifts expenses from a related manufacturer overseas will be disallowed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual CIT return attracts 20% of the unpaid tax as an unfaithful-return penalty under the Corporate Income Tax Act penalty provisions; underreported income attracts 10% penalty (20% if intentional concealment); delinquent tax accrues an additional monthly surcharge of 1.2% of the unpaid tax until settled. Failure to submit TP documentation attracts a separate penalty under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs of up to 20% of the undocumented international transaction amount in egregious cases. Fraudulent omission of income is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act: imprisonment up to 5 years and a criminal fine of up to five times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Aggregate 22% (20% corporate income tax withholding on the dividend payment to a non-resident, plus 2% local income tax surtax) where no treaty reduction applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced dividend WHT rate under a Korean foreign-investment treaty, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate of the treaty jurisdiction issued by the competent tax authority; (ii) submit the prescribed Application for Withholding Tax Reduction/Exemption to the Korean payer or the Korean district tax office before remittance; (iii) complete a beneficial-ownership statement confirming the recipient is the true owner of the dividends and is not contractually or practically required to pass them onward; and (iv) maintain evidence of share ownership period and financing/funding structure. The payer must retain the approved application with its withholding tax records. If tax is withheld at the statutory 22% and the treaty rate should have applied, the shareholder must file a refund claim through the Korean district tax office within the statutory limitation period, attaching the same DTA relief documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For outbound royalty payments, the domestic aggregate WHT is 22% (20% plus 2% local surtax); treaty rates usually reduce royalties to 10%-15% depending on the treaty. For outbound interest payments, domestic aggregate WHT is also 22%; most Korean DTAs cap interest at 10% for bank/disbursed loans and 15% for other interest, with some treaties allowing 0% under specific public/export-credit financing mechanisms. The same TRC and beneficial-ownership protocol applies to both royalty and interest WHT reductions; interest paid to a foreign controlling shareholder may also be recharacterized as equity under the Korean thin-capitalization rule.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in annual aggregate international related-party transactions for Local File; KRW 100 billion in annual aggregate international related-party transactions for Master File; transaction-level reporting threshold is set by the LCITA Enforcement Decree and currently applies to a company whose total international related-party transaction amount reaches KRW 50 billion, with both the Local and Master Files due by the CIT return date or evidence date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea is not a Gulf Cooperation Council ESR jurisdiction, so Economic Substance Regulations in the UAE/Bermuda/BVI sense do not apply. However, Korean tax courts apply an equivalent economic-substance and substance-over-form doctrine. For treaty benefits and transfer pricing defenses, the Korean LLC must prove that its core income-generating activities (manufacturing, inventory risk, procurement, warranty, and strategic management) are performed in Korea with real employees, physical facilities, and decision-making substance. A shell LLC without CIGA in Korea will lose DTA protection and be exposed to recharacterization of all related-party contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Omission of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors intentionally omit or understate export revenues from overseas electric-cargo-e-bike sales, create false purchase invoices with shell vendors, or route payments to non-resident personal accounts without recording the transfer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service assesses the omitted corporate income tax, adds 20% fraud penalty under the Corporate Income Tax Act penalty rules, applies monthly 1.2% delinquency surcharge, and refers the case to the public prosecutor. Conviction under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a criminal fine of at least 1 but not more than 5 times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 39 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, which serves as Korea's tax piercing-the-corporate-veil rule, a de facto or de jure director who controlled the evasion is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and surcharges. The director is subject to asset attachment and departure restriction (blacklisting/travel ban) when unpaid delinquent tax exceeds KRW 50 million. The personal criminal exposure is the same imprisonment term; restitution to the Treasury is ordered before other debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC distributes large dividends to a non-resident parent located in a treaty jurisdiction, but the parent is a paper company with no operations, no employees, no CIGA, and no commercial purpose other than obtaining a lower dividend withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean tax authority may deny treaty benefits under the domestic anti-treaty-shopping provision in the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and re-source the dividends as Korean-source income subject to full 22% aggregate withholding, plus additional penalties of 10%-20% for under-withheld tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act; criminal prosecution is possible for false declaration on the withholding relief form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the distribution without a valid relief form or with fraudulent TRC documents are personally liable for the shortfall as withholding agents, and can be pursued for the entire unreported tax. The director may be blacklisted (departure ban) and, for deliberate false documentation, prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act with imprisonment up to 5 years, plus parallel liability for Korean bank accounts and foreign assets under court seizure orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Profit Shifting to Tax Haven Affiliate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean manufacturer sells electric cargo e-bike components at artificially low prices to a foreign related distributor in a no-tax jurisdiction, or pays excessive synthetic royalty or management fees for already-bundled local technical services from a Hong Kong or Cayman IP affiliate, eroding the Korean taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service recomputes the arm's length price and assesses the resulting understated corporate tax. Penalties include a 20% negligent/unfaithful omission penalty (or 20% fraud penalty), a 10%-20% documentation failure penalty, and monthly delinquency surcharges. The tax authority may also disallow related-party royalty deductions under anti-abuse rules embedded in Korean law and impose an additional 10% penalty on the denied deduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who signed the intercompany pricing agreements is not protected by the fiction of separate personality: if the transfer pricing adjustment demonstrates deliberate fraud, the director is jointly liable under Article 39 of the Framework Act on National Taxes for the adjusted tax and penalties. Departure restrictions are imposed for delinquent tax over KRW 50 million; personal civil asset restitution and criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years attach when the tax authority proves criminal intent to cause tax loss.
